universities.summary: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) is a private self-financing dental college at Siruvachur, Perambalur, Tamil Nadu, admitting BDS students since 2021-22. It is affiliated to The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University, which awards its degree, and fills its 100 BDS seats through Tamil Nadu's NEET-based counselling.
universities.campusLifestyle: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) sits on about 7 acres on the Trichy-Chennai highway (NH-45) at Siruvachur, beside Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Medical College and Hospital. It runs nine clinical departments, from prosthodontics and orthodontics to oral and maxillofacial surgery, with outpatient and inpatient dental clinics. The campus has a library, hostel, cafeteria, auditorium, gymnasium, sports facilities and Wi-Fi.
universities.cityProfile: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) is at NH-45, Trichy-Chennai Highway, Siruvachur, Perambalur 621 113, Tamil Nadu, in Perambalur district of central Tamil Nadu. Perambalur town lies a few kilometres along the highway; Tiruchirappalli, about 60 km south on NH-45, has the nearest airport, and Ariyalur has the nearest major railway station. The college shares its Siruvachur location with the group's medical college and nursing college.
universities.practicalExposure: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) trains BDS students in its own outpatient and inpatient dental clinics across nine departments: prosthodontics and crown and bridge, periodontology, conservative dentistry and endodontics, orthodontics, public health dentistry, oral pathology, paediatric and preventive dentistry, oral medicine and radiology, and oral and maxillofacial surgery. The course ends with a one-year compulsory rotatory residential internship. The college runs oral screening camps and continuing dental education workshops. By Department of Higher Education notification 9-13/2026-U.3(A) of 24 August 2026, the college is one of three Siruvachur institutions that together form Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Institute of Science and Research (DSISR), an institution deemed to be university. The 2026-27 batch was admitted under the M.G.R. Medical University; admissions from 2027-28 are expected to move to DSISR once the dental regulator records the change.
universities.hostelOverview: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) has hostel accommodation on campus. In its pre-counselling fee disclosure to the Tamil Nadu Selection Committee for 2026-27, the college lists hostel fees of INR 12,500 a month and no transport charge. Room types and sharing are not published, so ask the college before reporting.
universities.dietarySupport: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) lists mess charges of INR 5,000 a month in its 2026-27 fee disclosure, and the campus has a cafeteria. The college does not publish a menu or say whether vegetarian-only or special diets are available, so ask the hostel office before joining.
universities.safetyOverview: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) has an anti-ragging committee, an anti-drug-abuse committee, an anti-discrimination committee and a student grievance redressal committee, named in its dental-commission disclosure. It holds an anti-ragging orientation programme for new students.
universities.studentSupport: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) has a student welfare committee, a monitoring committee and a hostel committee, plus academic, research and cultural councils. SC, SCA and ST management-quota students with family income below INR 2.5 lakh need not pay tuition upfront at counselling. Students Traffic counsellors can help you plan NEET choices and BDS fees.
whyChoose: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC)'s government-quota BDS fee is INR 2,50,000 a year for 2026-27, fixed by Tamil Nadu's Fee Fixation Committee.
DSDC's published hostel and mess charges for 2026-27 are INR 12,500 and INR 5,000 a month, lower than the neighbouring medical college's.
DSDC is on the same Siruvachur site as Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Medical College and Hospital, on the NH-45 Chennai-Trichy highway.
thingsToConsider: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) admits only through the Tamil Nadu Selection Committee on NEET-UG merit; government-quota seats need Tamil Nadu nativity, and there is no direct or foreign-national admission.
DSDC is a young college whose first BDS batch joined in 2021-22, and it offers no MDS course, so students who want to specialise must move elsewhere after BDS.
DSDC is now part of DSISR (deemed to be university) under the 24 August 2026 notification; the 2026-27 batch takes M.G.R. Medical University degrees, but later batches may be admitted under DSISR.

faq.question: Is Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College recognised?
faq.answer: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) is affiliated to The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University (institution code 943) with a sanctioned BDS intake of 100, and its BDS seats are offered in the Tamil Nadu Selection Committee's 2026-27 counselling. The college states that it is recognised by the National Dental Commission.

faq.question: What is the BDS fee at Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College?
faq.answer: For 2026-27 the Tamil Nadu Fee Fixation Committee set the annual BDS fee at self-financing dental colleges, including Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC), at INR 2,50,000 for government quota, INR 6,00,000 for management quota and INR 9,00,000 for NRI quota. Hostel (INR 12,500 a month) and mess (INR 5,000 a month) are extra.

faq.question: How do I get BDS admission at Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College?
faq.answer: Qualify NEET-UG and apply to the Tamil Nadu Selection Committee at tnmedicalselection.org. Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) says admission is done through the Secretary, Selection Committee, Directorate of Medical Education, Chennai. Government-quota seats need Tamil Nadu nativity; management-quota seats are open to Indian citizens and OCI/PIO holders.

faq.question: Which university is Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College affiliated to?
faq.answer: Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) is affiliated to The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University, Chennai, which awards its BDS degree. By the 24 August 2026 notification it is also a constituent of Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Institute of Science and Research (DSISR), a deemed university; admissions from 2027-28 are expected under DSISR.

faq.question: How long is the BDS course at Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College?
faq.answer: The BDS at Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) takes five years: four academic years followed by a one-year compulsory rotatory residential internship, as set out in the college's admission page and the Selection Committee's prospectus.

faq.question: Does Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College offer MDS?
faq.answer: No. Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) lists only BDS, with an approved intake of 100, in its dental-commission disclosure, and it does not appear in the Selection Committee's 2026-27 MDS prospectus for self-financing dental colleges.

faq.question: Can NRI students join Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College?
faq.answer: The Tamil Nadu Selection Committee fills NRI-quota BDS seats at self-financing dental colleges such as Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC), at INR 9,00,000 a year for 2026-27. NRI candidates need an Indian passport or eligible OCI card and an NRI parent or listed blood-relative sponsor. There is no separate route for other foreign nationals.

faq.question: Does Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College have a hostel?
faq.answer: Yes. Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College (DSDC) lists hostel fees of INR 12,500 a month and mess charges of INR 5,000 a month in its 2026-27 fee disclosure, with no transport charge.

fee.notes: Government-quota seat, 2026-27: INR 2,50,000 a year, the annual fee fixed by Tamil Nadu's Fee Fixation Committee for all self-financing dental colleges, covering tuition and recurring college charges. Hostel and mess are extra.

additionalFees.notes: Management-quota seat for Indian citizens and OCI/PIO candidates, 2026-27: INR 6,00,000 a year as fixed by Tamil Nadu's Fee Fixation Committee for all self-financing dental colleges. Hostel and mess are extra.

NRI-quota seat, 2026-27: INR 9,00,000 a year as fixed by Tamil Nadu's Fee Fixation Committee. Open only to NRI wards meeting the Selection Committee's NRI sponsorship rules, not to every foreign national. Hostel and mess are extra.

eligibleAudiences: Indian citizens who are natives of Tamil Nadu (government-quota seats through the Tamil Nadu Selection Committee)
Indian citizens and OCI/PIO card holders who qualify NEET-UG (management-quota seats through the Tamil Nadu Selection Committee)
Children or wards of Non-Resident Indians who meet the Selection Committee's NRI rules (NRI-quota seats)
restrictions: Every seat is allotted by the Secretary, Selection Committee, Directorate of Medical Education, Chennai on NEET-UG 2026 merit; the college makes no direct admissions.
Government-quota seats require a Tamil Nadu nativity certificate; candidates from other states can compete only for management-quota seats.
NRI-quota candidates must hold an Indian passport or an eligible OCI card and be sponsored by an NRI parent or listed blood relative; there is no general foreign-national route.

admissionsContent.overview: The B.D.S. at Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College, Siruvachur, is a five-year course (four academic years plus a one-year compulsory rotatory internship) with a sanctioned intake of 100. The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University awards the degree. All seats are filled by the Tamil Nadu Selection Committee on NEET-UG merit.

eligibility.intro: The Tamil Nadu Selection Committee's 2026-27 MBBS/BDS prospectuses set these conditions for BDS at Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College.
items: Indian citizen, or OCI/PIO card holder (open category only, no reservation)
At least 17 years old on or before 31 December 2026
Pass in Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English, with 50% in PCB together (40% SC/ST/OBC; 45% general PwBD)
NEET-UG 2026 at or above the 50th percentile (40th for SC/ST/OBC; 45th for general PwBD)
Tamil Nadu nativity certificate for government-quota seats
NRI quota: NRI sponsor, Indian passport or eligible OCI card, 50% in Biology and 50% each in Physics and Chemistry

applicationSteps: Qualify NEET-UG 2026 conducted by the National Testing Agency
Apply online at tnmedicalselection.org: the government-quota application (fee INR 500) and, separately, the management/NRI-quota application (fee INR 1,000); both opened on 29 June 2026
Upload the NEET admit card, Class 10, 11 and 12 mark sheets, transfer certificate and any community, nativity or NRI documents with the application
Register for online counselling; management-quota registration needs a refundable security deposit of INR 1,00,000 (INR 30,000 for government quota in self-financing colleges)
Choose Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College, Perambalur in choice filling and, on allotment, pay the fee online before downloading the allotment order
Report to the college at Siruvachur with the allotment order and original certificates by the stated date

academic: NEET-UG 2026 admit card and score card
application: Tamil Nadu nativity certificate, for government-quota seats
NRI quota: sponsor's NRI status certificate from the Indian Embassy, relationship certificate, sponsor's passport and NRE account passbook

admissionsContent.deadlinesNote: The 2026-27 BDS round is under way: the Selection Committee notified both prospectuses on 29 June 2026 and was running stray-vacancy rounds in October 2026. The college advertises its BDS 2026-2027 batch.

programmes.feeNotes: Annual fee fixed by Tamil Nadu's Committee on Fixation of Fee for self-financing professional colleges for 2026-27 BDS admissions at every self-financing dental college, including Dhanalakshmi Srinivasan Dental College: INR 2,50,000 a year for a government-quota seat, INR 6,00,000 a year for a management-quota seat and INR 9,00,000 a year for an NRI-quota seat. The committee's fee covers tuition and recurring college charges; hostel and mess are extra. The college's 2026 fee disclosure lists hostel at INR 12,500 a month and mess at INR 5,000 a month, no transport charge, and other fees as fixed by the Fee Fixation Committee.
